record.paper_title: The Hidden Subgroup Problem - Review and Open Problems
record.original_question: Is there a choice of basis for the irreducible representations of S_n or other nonabelian groups that makes quantum Fourier sampling informative enough to solve the hidden subgroup problem efficiently, despite the known failure of random-basis choices?

evidence.quote: For example, it is known the standard method cannot solve the HSP over Sn if the basis choice is random - it will take a clever basis choice for the irreducibles to obtain an efficient algorithm.
Yet there is hope that a clever basis choice for the irreducible representations might turn this around.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a finite nonabelian group (for instance the symmetric group $S_n$), and let $H \leq G$ be an unknown subgroup. A function $f : G \to S$ (with $S$ a finite set) is said to hide $H$ if $f$ is constant on each left coset of $H$ and distinct on different cosets. The hidden subgroup problem (HSP) asks for a quantum algorithm that, given oracle access to such an $f$, determines $H$ using time polynomial in $\log |G|$.

The standard (strong) quantum Fourier sampling procedure prepares a uniform superposition of coset representatives, applies the quantum Fourier transform over $G$, and measures. The outcome consists of an irreducible representation $\rho \in \widehat{G}$ together with row/column indices in $\rho$ that depend on the chosen orthonormal basis for the representation space of $\rho$. It is known that for $G = S_n$, if for each irreducible $\rho$ one fixes a basis chosen uniformly at random (Haar-distributed) inside $\rho$, then the resulting measurement statistics contain (with high probability) only an exponentially small amount of information about $H$, so no efficient algorithm based on this procedure can succeed.

Question: Does there exist, for $G = S_n$ (or for some other family of nonabelian groups for which HSP is not currently known to be efficiently solvable), an explicit, efficiently computable choice of orthonormal basis for each irreducible representation $\rho \in \widehat{G}$ such that the strong quantum Fourier sampling measurement, performed in these bases, produces an outcome distribution from which the hidden subgroup $H$ can be reconstructed by a (classical or quantum) algorithm running in time polynomial in $\log |G|$?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem remains open. Subsequent work showed that strong Fourier sampling with a random (Haar) basis fails for the symmetric group ("The Symmetric Group Defies Strong Fourier Sampling," Moore–Russell–Schulman), and even multi-register/entangled measurements have known limitations. While clever basis choices have been shown to suffice for some semidirect-product (affine, q-hedral) groups, no explicit basis for the irreducibles of S_n is known that makes Fourier sampling efficient for HSP, and an efficient quantum algorithm for HSP over S_n (which would imply an algorithm for graph isomorphism on the quantum side) is not known.

status_evidence.title: The Symmetric Group Defies Strong Fourier Sampling
status_evidence.snippet: Under general conditions, both weak and random-strong forms of quantum Fourier sampling fail to give advantage over classical exhaustive search for the symmetric group.
status_evidence.claim: Random basis choices for S_n fail; the problem of finding a clever basis remains.

status_evidence.title: The Power of Basis Selection in Fourier Sampling: Hidden Subgroup Problems in Affine Groups
status_evidence.snippet: Clever basis choices yield efficient algorithms for affine/q-hedral groups via strong Fourier sampling.
status_evidence.claim: Basis selection works for certain semidirect-product groups, but not known for S_n.

status_evidence.title: Hidden subgroup problem - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: An efficient quantum algorithm for the HSP for the symmetric group would give an efficient quantum algorithm for graph isomorphism; no such algorithm is known.
status_evidence.claim: HSP over S_n remains an open problem.
